claims.text: Changing the percentages of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr in HfNbTaTiZr HEA will significantly affect its mechanical properties.
Composition changes affect mechanical properties by altering lattice distortion.
Composition changes affect mechanical properties by altering atomic bonding.
The relevant strengthening mechanisms are solid-solution strengthening and lattice-strain hardening.
A composition variation within the proposed range will produce a 20% increase in yield strength relative to the equiatomic alloy.
A composition variation within the proposed range will produce a 15% improvement in ductility relative to the equiatomic alloy.
The baseline alloy contains 20 at.% each of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr.
The proposed composition domain places each constituent between 15 and 25 at.%.
Casting technique and post-processing treatments can alter the alloy's microstructure and mechanical properties.
Systematic elemental-composition variation, tensile testing, and microstructural analysis can be used to evaluate constituent effects on mechanical properties.
